opening.text: Pixelheim. A village under a mountain, and glad of it.
Then the Ashen Mountain woke, and Fafnyr with it.
In one night he burned Pixelheim to the ground.
Heroes climbed for its hoard. None came back.
And now the whispers come from below.

fafnyr.sub: He has slept on the hoard for a hundred years.

fafnyr.text: The summit is his. So is everything the heroes carried up.

descent.text: Fafnyr's last breath rattles out of him, and with it, words.

descent.sub: "...promised me your village. It lied - to us both."

descent.text: Behind the hoard, a stairway runs down into the dark.

morvax.sub: Once a hero of Pixelheim. Now its oldest debt.

morvax.text: "I carried a letter," you say. "You broke a seal."
Below the hoard, the dead keep their own court.

ending.text: You bring the blade down. Morvax the Deathless breaks like old glass, and the dark takes what is left of him.
{hero} slew Fafnyr the Ashen above and destroyed Morvax the Deathless below.
The mountain is quiet at last, the tavern is loud, and the cheese has never tasted better.

after: and Infinite Cheese Wheels as themselves

crypt.text: Behind the Barrow Crypt's guardian: three graves under one stone, and a fourth name chiselled away.

crypt.sub: of the Ember Five, who held the stair.

crypt.text: On the wall above them hangs a shield, its paint gone grey: MORVAX OF PIXELHEIM.

forge.text: The Sunken Forge's great mould is cold. Something was cast here once - a disc of black iron the size of a cartwheel.
On the anvil lies its twin: an old seal, cracked clean through.
The crack runs from beneath. Someone broke it from below.

dream_courier.text: You dream of a stair, going down and down, and of something waiting at the bottom.
You wake to the smell of smoke and Sela snoring.

dream_five.text: You dream of five torches climbing the mountain in the dark.
"Five went up. Four came down. One went further."
One by one, four torches go out.

dream_door.text: You dream of a great door in the mountain, and of a dragon asleep against it.
"The dragon was only ever my door, courier. Thank you for opening it."
You wake with your hand on your sword.

ending_rest.text: You read him Liane's last page. When you say their names - Tam, Oskar, Liane, Maren - Morvax lowers his hands.
"Tell Maren... she was right to run." Then he is only dust, and the dead around the throne lie down.
{hero} slew Fafnyr the Ashen above and laid Morvax, once a hero of Pixelheim, to rest below.
Five lanterns burn on the square tonight. The tavern is loud, and the cheese has never tasted better.

after: and Infinite Cheese Wheels as themselves

lore.title: Page I
lore.text: We set out at first light, five of us, to renew the Ember Seal. Morvax says it will hold another hundred years once it's done. Tam brought cheese. Of course Tam brought cheese.

lore.title: Page II
lore.text: The crypt is older than the village. I read the walls: kings were buried here before the mountain had a name. Morvax lingered by the gold. He always lingers by the gold.

lore.title: Page III
lore.text: Frosthowl. Oskar carried me the last mile and complained the whole way. Maren laughed for the first time since we left. I'm writing that down so I remember it.

lore.title: Page IV
lore.text: The old seal is cracking. It sits on Fafnyr's chain, a disc of black iron, warm like something asleep. We have to forge a new one in the Sunken Forge and carry it up.

lore.title: Page V
lore.text: We cast the new seal from the old one's mould. Morvax watched the fire for a long time and said: 'Imagine what else could be forged down here.' Nobody answered him.

lore.title: Page VI
lore.text: Fafnyr sleeps. It took all five of us to lift the seal onto the chain. Then Morvax found a stair behind the hoard, going down.

lore.title: Page VII
lore.text: He says the deep holds a power to rebuild the old kingdom. Oskar told him kingdoms are built of people, not gold. They haven't spoken since.

lore.title: Page VIII
lore.text: We followed him down. I wish we hadn't. The dead don't stay dead here. They wait, and they listen to him.

lore.title: Page IX
lore.text: I'm writing in the dark. Tam fell holding the stair. Oskar is still fighting. I told Maren to run, and she ran. Good. Morvax didn't even look back.

lore.title: Page X
lore.text: If anyone finds this: Maren got out. Tell her it wasn't her fault. Tell her to seal the stair. - Liane

lines: Tam's ladle. Gods. He cooked for us all the way up - stew on a mountain, in the snow.
He said a hero who eats well fights well. He was the first to laugh and the first to stand when it went wrong.
Wenna's brother. I should have gone down to Saltmere years ago and told her. I'll go. When this is done, I'll go.
Black iron with our five marks on it. We dug the seal's iron at Blackiron ourselves.
Oskar swung the pick, Liane did the sums, Tam fed the miners and Morvax paid. I set my mark last.
I was so proud of that mark. Look at it. Still there.
Oskar's shield. He left it at Greyhold and told his captain to keep it till he came home.
He carried Liane the last mile up and complained the whole way. And Hale kept it fifty years?
...Of course he did. That was Greyhold.
Her lantern. Liane lit it the night before we climbed and said she'd blow it out herself when we were all home.
She wrote everything down, you know. Every day of it.
If you find her pages up there, read them. She'd want someone to.
You found the graves in the crypt. Oskar, Liane, Tam.
Old names. Old graves. Leave them be, courier - some names are heavier than they look.
Sit. You've earned the story. The Ember Seal: black iron, forged in the Sunken Forge, set on Fafnyr's chain at the top of the mountain.
It kept him asleep a hundred years. Fifty years ago it cracked, and five fools climbed to make a new one.
I was one of the five. Don't look at me like that. Climb, and you'll understand.
Fafnyr spoke of a voice below. I know whose voice.
There were five of us. Morvax led. When the seal was set, he went down the stair behind the hoard, and we followed him.
Tam, Liane, Oskar - they held the stair so I could run. I came home alone and called it a rockfall. Fifty years I've called it a rockfall.
He isn't dead, courier. He's waiting. Go down and end it - for them, if not for me.
He said I was right to run? ...Then maybe I can stop running.
Sit with me a while. The fire's warm, and for once the mountain is quiet.
So he's gone. Truly gone.
Fifty years I hated him, courier. I thought I'd feel lighter when he was dust. ...Maybe tomorrow.
Go on, the festival is for you. I'll sit by the fire a while.
